title: memory.rs Inner: HashMap lookups allocate a String on every read via .to_owned() on account_id
description:
Sites: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs:107-150 (Inner::current_state, bump_state, objects_mut, objects_ref, change_log_mut). Same pattern repeats at 528, 588-599 and throughout the file (45 .clone() and ~10 .to_owned() call sites).

Current code (objects_ref is the read-only canary):

    fn objects_ref(
        &self,
        type_name: &'static str,
        account_id: &str,
    ) -> Option<&HashMap<Id, serde_json::Value>> {
        self.objects.get(&(type_name, account_id.to_owned()))
    }

The HashMap key is (&'static str, String). Every lookup, mutating or not, constructs a fresh String to make the temporary tuple lookup key. The .to_owned() allocates a heap buffer and immediately drops it after .get() returns. current_state, objects_ref, and the get-only paths called from query/get/changes all do this on every wire-level method call, multiplied by every object type the dispatcher routes.

What idiomatic Rust does: either (a) restructure as a nested map HashMap<&'static str, HashMap<String, ...>> so the outer key never needs to be owned for lookup and the inner key can be borrowed via the standard Borrow<str>-on-String path; or (b) keep the tuple shape but use a key type (&'static str, Box<str>) with a custom Borrow<(&'static str, str)> impl so .get() can take &(&'static str, &str) without allocating. Option (a) is the conventional Rust solution and the one a senior Rust practitioner would expect to see in a reference impl.

What goes wrong if left: maintainability — the gratuitous-allocation pattern is the kind of thing that gets propagated into downstream backends that copy this code as a starting point. The pattern says 'don't think about ownership; clone your way out.' The fix is mechanical and a one-time cost; the cost of leaving it gets paid by every reader and every downstream copy.

This finding is the textbook 'gratuitous clone' pattern from the rusty pass error-handling/ownership section. The earlier rusty pass at JMAP-x2gd notes (2026-05-14 03:22, idiom rating ACCEPTABLE) explicitly said memory.rs was skipped: 'I read all handler-level src files but only sampled backend.rs (789 lines) and skipped memory.rs entirely (3121 lines)'. This is one of the misses that confidence note flagged.

Per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' rule: crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs is the canonical extension-server template (2742 lines) and almost certainly carries the same pattern. If propagated, change mail-server's memory.rs first and propagate here; if it does not carry the pattern, this is chat-server-local drift and the fix is local. Spawn an explore agent or grep mail-server to determine which before fixing.
